video_title: Why REST Exists: Resources Not Remote Procedures
core_insight: REST is a constraint set for using HTTP as an application protocol, shifting from remote procedures to resources identified by URIs and manipulated with standard verbs, enabling evolvable, cacheable, decoupled APIs.

scenes.voice: Why do we still talk about REST in 2025? Because the web itself forces a problem.
scenes.visual: Split screen: left shows early web API with POST /api/execute and JSON action field, right shows modern browser, mobile app, partner integration icons.

scenes.voice: Early APIs used RPC over HTTP. One endpoint, custom action names in the body. Clients had to know the exact operation set, and servers kept session state.
scenes.visual: Simple diagram of client sending {action:'createOrder'} to /api/execute, server maintaining session.
scenes.on_screen_text: RPC over HTTP couples client to operations

scenes.voice: That breaks on the web. HTTP is stateless, cacheable, and has a uniform interface. Clients and servers evolve independently across networks and teams.
scenes.visual: Icons for stateless, cache, proxies, multiple languages.

scenes.voice: REST changes the question. Stop asking what can I do, start asking what resource and what state change. Resources are nouns with URIs: orders/123, users/me.
scenes.visual: Noun to URI mapping, GET /orders/123 highlighted.

scenes.voice: The uniform interface uses standard verbs. GET retrieves, POST creates, PUT/PATCH updates, DELETE removes. Every request is self-contained, no server session.
scenes.visual: Mermaid sequence showing GET then PATCH.

scenes.voice: What do we gain? Any HTTP client works, GET responses are cacheable by CDNs and proxies, servers scale horizontally because they are stateless, and clients and servers can evolve without coordinated releases.
scenes.visual: CDN caching GET, horizontal server replicas, independent version arrows.

scenes.voice: What do we sacrifice? Standard verbs are less expressive for complex workflows, statelessness repeats auth on every call, and resources can cause over or under fetching. No built-in transactions.
scenes.visual: Trade-off balance scale: Uniformity vs Expressiveness, Stateless vs Session memory.

scenes.voice: Use REST for public, web-facing, long-lived APIs where interoperability and caching matter. Prefer RPC or GraphQL for internal high-performance or fine-grained needs.
scenes.visual: Decision flow: Public/long-lived -> REST, Internal/high TPS -> gRPC.

mental_model: Think resources with URIs and standard HTTP verbs, not remote procedures. Ask what state transition on a named resource you need, not what operation to invoke. Constraints enable caching, scaling, and independent evolution.
final_takeaway: REST is constraints on HTTP for evolvable APIs, not a framework. It buys decoupling and cacheability at the cost of expressiveness.
